items.stem: What is the core idea of the strangler fig pattern for modernization?

options.text: Incrementally route functionality to a new system while the old one keeps running, retiring it gradually
options.rationale: Correct: the strangler fig replaces the legacy system piece by piece, reducing risk.

options.text: Rewrite the whole application at once and switch over in a single release
options.rationale: That is a big-bang migration, the opposite of the strangler fig.

options.text: Freeze the legacy app and never change it again
options.rationale: Freezing is not migration; the pattern is about gradual replacement.

options.text: Duplicate the database and hope both stay in sync forever
options.rationale: The pattern is about routing functionality, not indefinite data duplication.

items.explanation: Correct: the strangler fig replaces the legacy system piece by piece, reducing risk.

items.stem: Select TWO factors that should drive the choice between rehost, refactor and re-architect.

options.text: The business driver and acceptable risk/effort for each application
options.rationale: Correct: strategy follows business drivers and the risk/effort a team can accept.

options.text: Which legacy dependencies have modern equivalents or blockers
options.rationale: Correct: compatibility blockers strongly influence a feasible strategy.

options.text: The color scheme of the admin UI
options.rationale: Cosmetic UI details do not determine a modernization strategy.

options.text: Whichever option a vendor markets most aggressively
options.rationale: Vendor marketing is not a sound basis for the decision.

options.text: Choosing re-architect always, regardless of context
options.rationale: A blanket choice ignores the trade-offs the decision is meant to weigh.

items.explanation: Correct: strategy follows business drivers and the risk/effort a team can accept.

items.stem: Why is "lift and shift" (rehost) not automatically the same as modernizing the codebase?

options.text: It moves the app to new infrastructure but leaves the application code and its debt largely unchanged
options.rationale: Correct: rehosting changes hosting, not the code; modernization of the code is a separate effort.

options.text: It always rewrites the code to the latest framework
It deletes the legacy code entirely
options.rationale: Rehost preserves the code; it does not delete it.

options.text: It guarantees the app becomes cloud-native
options.rationale: Rehosting alone does not make an app cloud-native.

items.explanation: Correct: rehosting changes hosting, not the code; modernization of the code is a separate effort.
